questions.questionText: What is the purpose of cache memory near the CPU?
options: Store frequently used data for faster access
Archive rarely used files for long-term preservation
questions.correctAnswer: Store frequently used data for faster access
questions.explanation: Cache keeps frequently needed instructions and data close to the processor, reducing average access time.

curriculum.objective: Analyse computer architecture, virtualization, cloud services and performance trade-offs for organizational requirements.

questions.questionText: Which cloud model provides virtual machines, storage and networking while the customer manages the operating system?
options: Fully managed Software as a Service
questions.correctAnswer: Infrastructure as a Service
questions.explanation: IaaS supplies virtualized infrastructure, while the customer typically controls the operating system and deployed applications.

curriculum.objective: Analyse computer architecture, virtualization, cloud services and performance trade-offs for organizational requirements.

questions.questionText: Why can adding CPU cores fail to double an application’s speed?
options: Every task becomes perfectly parallel when extra cores are added
Some tasks are sequential or limited by other resources
questions.correctAnswer: Some tasks are sequential or limited by other resources
questions.explanation: Parallel speed-up is limited by sequential work and bottlenecks such as memory, storage or synchronization.

curriculum.objective: Analyse computer architecture, virtualization, cloud services and performance trade-offs for organizational requirements.

questions.questionText: An organization runs several isolated servers on one physical machine. What technology enables this most directly?
questions.correctAnswer: Hypervisor-based virtualization
questions.explanation: A hypervisor allocates physical resources among isolated virtual machines, allowing multiple server environments on one host.

curriculum.objective: Analyse computer architecture, virtualization, cloud services and performance trade-offs for organizational requirements.

questions.questionText: What does a subnet mask determine in an IPv4 network?
options: Which address bits identify network and host
The encryption key for every packet
The physical length of a cable
questions.correctAnswer: Which address bits identify network and host
questions.explanation: The mask separates the network prefix from the host portion so devices can determine whether a destination is local.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate network designs, cryptographic controls, authentication and incident responses against advanced threats and operational needs.

questions.questionText: Why are passwords normally stored as salted hashes?
options: To make passwords readable by administrators
To resist password recovery and precomputed attacks
To guarantee users choose unique usernames
questions.correctAnswer: To resist password recovery and precomputed attacks
questions.explanation: Hashing avoids storing plaintext, and a unique salt makes identical passwords differ and defeats many precomputed hash tables.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate network designs, cryptographic controls, authentication and incident responses against advanced threats and operational needs.

questions.questionText: What security property does a digital signature primarily provide?
options: Authenticity and integrity of the signed data
questions.correctAnswer: Authenticity and integrity of the signed data
questions.explanation: A valid digital signature shows that the holder of the private key signed the data and that it has not been altered.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate network designs, cryptographic controls, authentication and incident responses against advanced threats and operational needs.

questions.questionText: After ransomware is detected on one workstation, what is the best immediate containment action?
options: Isolate the affected device from the network
questions.correctAnswer: Isolate the affected device from the network
questions.explanation: Network isolation limits lateral spread while preserving the device for investigation and coordinated recovery.

curriculum.objective: Evaluate network designs, cryptographic controls, authentication and incident responses against advanced threats and operational needs.

questions.questionText: What does a foreign key represent in a relational database?
options: A reference to a key in another table
An encrypted copy of every record
A field that must contain decimal values
questions.correctAnswer: A reference to a key in another table
questions.explanation: A foreign key links related rows by referencing a candidate or primary key in another table.

curriculum.objective: Design relational databases, use queries and transactions, and evaluate data quality and analytical conclusions.

questions.questionText: Which transaction property ensures committed data survives a system failure?
questions.correctAnswer: Durability
questions.explanation: Durability means that once a transaction commits, its changes persist even after a crash or power loss.

curriculum.objective: Design relational databases, use queries and transactions, and evaluate data quality and analytical conclusions.

questions.questionText: Which SQL operation combines related rows from customers and orders using a shared customer ID?
questions.correctAnswer: JOIN
questions.explanation: A JOIN combines rows from tables using a relationship condition such as matching customer identifiers.

curriculum.objective: Design relational databases, use queries and transactions, and evaluate data quality and analytical conclusions.

questions.questionText: A dashboard shows sales rising after an advertising campaign. Why does this alone not prove the campaign caused the rise?
options: Other variables may explain the correlation
questions.correctAnswer: Other variables may explain the correlation
questions.explanation: A time association is correlation, and seasonality, pricing or other changes may be confounding causes.

curriculum.objective: Design relational databases, use queries and transactions, and evaluate data quality and analytical conclusions.

questions.questionText: What is decomposition in software development?
options: Breaking a complex problem into smaller parts
Combining every function into one statement
Converting source code into an image
questions.correctAnswer: Breaking a complex problem into smaller parts
questions.explanation: Decomposition makes a complex system manageable by dividing it into modules or subproblems with clearer responsibilities.

curriculum.objective: Apply decomposition, algorithms, version control and systematic testing to develop maintainable software solutions.

questions.questionText: What is the main benefit of version control branching?
options: Prevent any previous version from being recovered
Store passwords directly in source files
questions.correctAnswer: Develop changes independently before integration
questions.explanation: Branches isolate work so features or fixes can be reviewed and tested before they are merged into the shared codebase.

curriculum.objective: Apply decomposition, algorithms, version control and systematic testing to develop maintainable software solutions.

questions.questionText: Which test best verifies that two modules exchange data correctly?
options: Unit test of one isolated function
questions.correctAnswer: Integration test
questions.explanation: Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions between components after their individual behavior is tested.

curriculum.objective: Apply decomposition, algorithms, version control and systematic testing to develop maintainable software solutions.

questions.questionText: An algorithm repeatedly halves a sorted search range. What is its time complexity?
questions.correctAnswer: O(log n)
questions.explanation: Binary search halves the remaining range each step, so the number of comparisons grows logarithmically with input size.

curriculum.objective: Apply decomposition, algorithms, version control and systematic testing to develop maintainable software solutions.

questions.questionText: What is a disaster-recovery plan designed to support?
options: Restoration of critical services after disruption
Permanent removal of all backup copies
questions.correctAnswer: Restoration of critical services after disruption
questions.explanation: A disaster-recovery plan defines people, procedures and resources for restoring priority technology services after serious disruption.

questions.questionText: Why is an audit trail important in an information system?
options: It makes every user an administrator
It records actions for accountability and investigation
It guarantees data is always unbiased
questions.correctAnswer: It records actions for accountability and investigation
questions.explanation: Audit logs provide evidence of who performed actions and when, supporting monitoring, investigation and compliance.

questions.questionText: An automated hiring model rejects applicants from one demographic at a much higher rate. What should the organization examine first?
options: Whether the interface uses animated icons
Whether every applicant owns the same device
Bias in data, features and decision thresholds
Whether the database name is short
questions.correctAnswer: Bias in data, features and decision thresholds
questions.explanation: Disparate outcomes can result from unrepresentative training data, proxy variables or thresholds, so these should be audited.

questions.questionText: A hospital is choosing between maximum data collection and patient privacy. Which approach is most defensible?
options: Collect everything because storage is inexpensive
Use purpose limitation, consent and proportionate safeguards
questions.correctAnswer: Use purpose limitation, consent and proportionate safeguards
questions.explanation: A defensible system limits processing to legitimate purposes, respects consent requirements and applies safeguards proportionate to risk.
